scenes.title: 1960 Harvard Tachistoscope: 50-ms '3×4 Letter Grid' Flash + Post-Flash High/Mid/Low Tone Revealing 9.1 of 12 Letters!

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1960 Harvard psychophysics laboratory featuring a clean white tabletop two-field **tachistoscope viewer**, an illuminated wall display replica of the **3×4 Consonant Grid ('T D R N / F Z K B / X L G M — 50 ms Flash')**, a three-tone audio generator (**High = Top Row, Mid = Middle Row, Low = Bottom Row**), and George Sperling's iconic **Decay Graph ('0 ms Delay: 9.1 Letters -> 500 ms Delay: 4.5 Letters')**.

positions.who: George Sperling (25-year-old mannequin in 1960 Oxford button-down shirt, slim tie, and tweed vest)
positions.where: triggering the 50-ms grid flash followed immediately after blackout by the 'High Tone' button while pointing to the steep 0-to-500-ms decay curve
positions.facing: standing beside tachistoscope and tone box

positions.who: Harvard Volunteer mannequin (in 1960 collegiate crewneck sweater)
positions.where: peering into the clean white tachistoscope hood, hearing the High Tone AFTER the flash goes dark, and crisply reciting 'T — D — R — N!' onto the response pad

props.name: 3×4 twelve-consonant stimulus grid board ('T D R N / F Z K B / X L G M')
props.period_detail: the exact 12-letter array that trapped psychology at 4.5 letters for 74 years
props.physical_behavior: lets viewers test their own eyes instantly

props.name: 3-Button Post-Flash Audio Tone Box ('HIGH 2500Hz -> Row 1 | MID 650Hz -> Row 2 | LOW 250Hz -> Row 3')
props.period_detail: sounds AFTER the screen goes dark so eyes cannot pre-aim

props.name: Iconic Decay Curve plaque ('9.1 Letters at 0s -> 4.5 Ceiling at 0.5s')
props.period_detail: plots the exact 300–500 ms evaporation of raw visual memory

actions.verb_sequence: flashes the 3×4 grid for 50 milliseconds -> screen drops dark -> triggers the High Tone at 0 ms delay -> Volunteer recites all 4 top-row letters effortlessly ('9.1 / 12 capacity!')
repeats waiting 0.5 seconds in the dark before sounding the tone -> Volunteer catches only 1–2 letters from that row as the curve hits the 4.5 floor

reactions.reaction: nods vindicated ('See! I really DID see all twelve for a split second!')
charts the birth of Sensory Iconic Memory

scenes.wardrobe: 1960 Ivy League attire: Oxford cloth button-down, slim knit tie, wool vest; collegiate crewneck sweater.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ask for all 12 flashed letters and everyone stalls at 4 — play a high or low beep AFTER the screen goes dark and suddenly you prove 9 letters were glowing inside the brain!

key_visual.description: a 1960 Harvard psychophysics desk with a white tachistoscope, a 3x4 twelve-consonant grid board, a High/Mid/Low post-flash audio tone generator, and a 9.1-to-4.5-letter 500ms decay graph

scenes.title: Bright Backward Masking vs Rapid Phone Scrolling

layout.description: Split comparison: a bright white post-flash wiping out Sperling's 3×4 ghost image vs a thumb flicking bright slides every 0.3 seconds.

positions.where: realizing why flicking through 30 bright slides in 15 seconds leaves zero retained memory

props.name: Backward-Masking Timeline card ('New Flash <300ms = Bleaches Previous Image')
props.period_detail: connects 1960 masking physics directly to modern feed-scrolling amnesia

actions.verb_sequence: slows down and pauses 2 full seconds on an important diagram so working memory copies it cleanly

scenes.recognition_hook: Every bright new slide you scroll onto your retina inside 300 milliseconds acts like bleach on the ghost image of the slide before it!

layout.description: Sunlit seminar stage comparing 'Phenomenal Overflow (All 12 Conscious)' vs 'Global Workspace Gate (Preconscious V1 -> 4 Conscious)'.

positions.where: pointing to Sperling's 1960 3×4 grid as Exhibit A in modern consciousness science

props.name: Overflow vs Workspace Gate diagram
props.period_detail: shows a 1960 student thesis still driving cutting-edge brain theory

actions.verb_sequence: trace V1 persistence vs frontoparietal P3b readout

scenes.recognition_hook: Sixty-five years later, the sharpest debate in consciousness science still revolves around George Sperling's twelve consonants!

scenes.title: Partial-Report Focus in Real Life: Grabbing the Last 4 License Digits

layout.description: Bright sidewalk where a witness glances once at a 7-character plate and immediately locks attention onto the final 4 characters.

positions.where: mentally cuing the right-hand 4 characters inside the 300-ms window and jotting them down 100% accurately

props.name: 4-character chunk notepad
props.physical_behavior: beats losing everything trying to grab all 7

actions.verb_sequence: aims mental spotlight at the last 4 characters immediately -> writes all 4 cleanly

scenes.recognition_hook: You only get 300 milliseconds before the ghost photograph fades — aim your mental spotlight at four priority digits first!
